subject: Re: Order Form SLA — operational exceptions & maintenance lifecycle
messages:

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@lucentlabs.com>
Date: 2024-04-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify SLA operational exceptions and maintenance lifecycle

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Our procurement and infra teams ran a pass and have three ask areas we need clarified before legal will sign: uptime measurement window, planned maintenance notification and carveouts for emergency security patches. Specifically: 

- How is uptime measured for multi-region deployments? Will a regional outage count as global downtime?
- We need a clear maximum for cumulative planned maintenance per quarter and a notification lead time.
- Emergency patching: we accept shorter notice in emergencies but need a formal process and a cap on frequency.

Can you propose concrete redline language for the Order Form (or point to the MSA section you rely on)? We want to avoid open-ended language that makes credits or SLAs hard to calculate.

Also, please attach any SOC2/evidence mapping we can send to our security team.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Infrastructure, Lucent Labs

---

Subject: Re: Clarify SLA operational exceptions and maintenance lifecycle

Alex — thanks for the clear points. I took a pass with the product and ops teams and drafted concrete redline language; attaching the Word redline and an evidence matrix. High-level proposal below so you can validate quickly before we hand to legal.

1) Uptime measurement (multi-region):
Proposed Order Form sentence: "Uptime is measured at the regional endpoint level and aggregated per Account using a weighted-average by region traffic share. For the avoidance of doubt, a degradation or outage confined to a single region will count only against that region's availability for the purposes of calculating Service Credits unless the Customer has configured global traffic failover that routes >75% of traffic through impacted region(s)."
Why: avoids counting a single-region maintenance as global downtime while protecting customers who rely on single-region routing.

2) Planned maintenance:
Proposed Order Form sentence: "Planned maintenance that may impact availability will be scheduled with no less than 72 hours' notice. Planned maintenance will not exceed 6 hours per region per calendar quarter, except where expressly agreed in writing. The Customer will be notified via email and the Console maintenance feed."
Why: clear numeric caps and channels for notification.

3) Emergency security patches (exceptions):
Proposed Order Form sentence: "Emergency security patches required to remediate zero-day vulnerabilities or active exploitation may be performed with shorter notice; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide prior notice or, if not feasible, post-event notification within 24 hours. Emergency patches are excluded from Planned Maintenance caps but will be included in Service Credit calculations only if they exceed 4 cumulative hours in any 30-day rolling window."
Why: balances speed with predictability and caps the operational impact.

4) Service Credits (clarity):
Proposed Order Form table (summary line): "If Account availability falls below 99.95% for a given calendar month at the Account level (traffic-weighted), Customer will be eligible for a Service Credit equal to 10% of monthly fee for each 0.1% below 99.95%, up to a maximum of 100% of the monthly fee. Credits are calculated after excluding Planned Maintenance and Emergency Patches as defined above."

Next steps I propose: Marissa / Jonas — can legal review the redline and confirm if MSA cross-references need amending? Jonas: if you want, I can mark the Word doc with the MSA section references (currently we rely on MSA §5.3 — Maintenance & Exceptions). Also attaching minimal evidence matrix (SOC2 scope, retention of audit logs, KMS notes) as requested.

If this looks directionally right to you Alex, we'll loop legal and procurement and send an updated orderform + DocuSign-ready link.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Alex — appreciate the clear asks and thanks Naomi for the detailed language. Two commercial notes: 

- We can accept the 6-hour/quarter planned maintenance cap per region as written, provided Lucent signs the attached redline and the Order Form's billing schedule remains unchanged.
- For the Service Credit ramp, we'd prefer a monthly cap of 50% of the monthly fee rather than 100% to align with precedent. If legal is comfortable, let's propose 50% cap in the Order Form and document exception flows for escalations.

Jonas — please prioritize legal review on the MSA cross-ref and the proposed Emergency Patch carveout. If you want, I can host a 30-min call with Lucent's procurement/legal tomorrow to walk through redlines. Naomi — can you prepare the DocuSign link after we lock the final cap?

Cheers,
Marissa
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks team and Alex. Quick legal read below; full redline will follow.

- MSA cross-reference: confirm MSA §5.3 and add a defined term in the Order Form: """Operational Exceptions" means Planned Maintenance, Emergency Patches, Force Majeure, and Customer-caused outages as defined in MSA §2.1."""

- Service Credit cap: Marissa, 50% monthly cap is acceptable from legal (reduces commercial risk). We'll mirror that cap into the credit calculation clause and add a sentence identifying the remediation process (credit request window: Customer must submit claim within 60 days of the end of the month; credits applied to next invoice).

- Evidence and security: Naomi — evidence_matrix_20240416.xlsx looks good; we'll redact any customer-specific markers and ship a SOC2 scope statement. Alex — Lucent's security team should confirm whether additional audit artifacts are needed; if so, we'll propose an NDA addendum for sharing more detailed logs (standard template).

I'll circulate a tracked-change MSA + Order Form packet by EOD tomorrow. Marissa — yes to the 30-min call; please share calendar options and I'll join.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
